name: Ferralive-4
description: Ferralive-4 is a high-tensile iron-carbon alloy threaded with a suspended culture of engineered fibroblast-analog cells housed within microscopic vascular channels pressed into the metal matrix during nano-assembly. When the alloy sustains surface damage, ruptured micro-channels release a clotting-analog fluid that oxidizes into a hard ceramic patch within 4-8 hours, restoring up to 85% of original tensile strength without external intervention. The material requires a low-level bioelectric charge from the host or an embedded power cell to keep the cell culture viable.
cost: Φ3,800 per kg (raw billet); Φ6,100 per kg (implant-interface grade)
story_hooks: A mercenary's Ferralive-4 arm chassis has been healing itself for three years without maintenance — but the fibroblast culture has mutated under repeated combat stress, and the patches it lays down are increasingly unlike the original alloy, with unknown long-term structural consequences.

Salvagers discover a cache of decommissioned Ferralive-4 armor plating that is still alive — the cell culture has survived for a decade on residual ambient bioelectricity, and the material has been slowly self-modifying in storage.

A Tier 1 street doc is offering black-market Ferralive-4 repairs using harvested cell cultures from expired medical waste — it works, but the donor cells carry unscreened genetic material that is integrating into recipients.
